column1: In hindsight this was a mistake:
- it complicated context allocation failure handling
/* kthread execs. TODO: cleanup this horror. */
- it caused us to enable irqs in fpu__restore():
* does a slab alloc which can sleep
- it (slightly) slowed down task creation/destruction by adding
- it made access to context contents (slightly) slower by adding
The motivation for the dynamic allocation was two-fold:
- reduce memory consumption by non-FPU tasks
- allocate and handle only the necessary amount of context for
various XSAVE processors that have varying hardware frame

column2: all non-kthread tasks have used the FPU shortly after

column1: instruction set - so they'll too often use the larger xstate frame
So remove the dynamic allocation complication by embedding the FPU
fpstate in task_struct again. This should make the FPU a lot more
accessible to all sorts of atomic contexts.
We could still optimize for the xstate frame size in the future
by moving the state structure to the last element of task_struct
and allocating only a part of that.
